Duration::to_note¶

Back to Duration API Reference

Signature¶

Note Duration::to_note() const;

Human-Readable Duration Text¶

to_note() converts every lane to fixed-field text of the form D days HH:MM:SS.nnnnnnnnn. It is intended for tabular display, labels, and text processing where aligned fields and explicit nanosecond precision are more useful than a compact interchange notation.

Negative spans use floor-normalized fields. Therefore -1 ns is represented as -1 days 23:59:59.999999999, not as a separate minus sign applied to every field. This is the same canonical decomposition exposed by days(), hours(), and the remaining component methods. NaT becomes the text lane "NaT".

The result is a newly allocated UTF-8 Note with exactly the receiver’s rank, shape, and lane order. It is text, not a borrowed view and not a reversible change to the receiver. Use to_note_iso() when another system expects ISO duration syntax instead.

Examples¶

Example 1. Positive, negative, zero, and absent values show the complete text contract.

auto values = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {93'784'005'006'007LL, -1, 0, pluss::Duration::kNaT});
std::cout << values.to_note();

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["1 days 02:03:04.005006007", "-1 days 23:59:59.999999999", "0 days 00:00:00.000000000", "NaT"]

Example 2. N-D structure survives conversion.

auto matrix = pluss::duration::nanos(
    {0, -1, 1'000'000'000, 86'400'000'000'000LL}, {2,2});
std::cout << matrix.to_note();

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["0 days 00:00:00.000000000", "-1 days 23:59:59.999999999"],
  ["0 days 00:00:01.000000000", "1 days 00:00:00.000000000"]
]

Example 3. Scalar input produces a scalar Note, not a one-element vector.

auto label = pluss::duration::minutes(90).to_note();
// label.dim() == 0, label.numel() == 1
